title: A Short, Urgent Cry for Help
overview: A person under attack begs God to hurry, asking that the mockers be stopped and that everyone who looks to God find joy.

parts.label: Hurry, God (v. 1)
parts.note: The psalm opens breathlessly, asking God twice to come quickly. Nearly the same words close Psalm 40, so this seems to be that ending reused as a short prayer for moments of crisis.

parts.label: Turn back the gloaters (vv. 2-3)
parts.note: The speaker faces people who want him dead and cheer his trouble with a mocking "Aha! Aha!" He asks that their plans fail and that they back off in embarrassment.

parts.label: Joy for those who seek God (v. 4)
parts.note: The focus widens from one person's danger to everyone who looks to God for rescue. The hope is that they will have reason to celebrate and keep saying out loud how great God is.

parts.label: Poor, needy, still waiting (v. 5)
parts.note: "Poor and needy" here means helpless and out of options, not only short of money. The psalm ends without an answer, still asking God not to delay.

think: When you have needed help urgently and it did not come right away, what did the waiting do to you?
